knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=Non-redundant peptide spectrum matches (psmSet object) from read.bibliospec ;; data.fit=Redundant peptide spectrum matches (psmSet object) containing iRT peptides used for building the RT normalization model ;; max.mZ.Da.error=Maximum MS2 tolerance in Da (e.g., 0.05) ;; topN=The N most intense fragment ions to keep (e.g., 6) ;; fragmentIonMzRange=mZ range filter of fragment ions (e.g., c(300, 1250)) ;; fragmentIonRange=Min/max number of fragment ions (e.g., c(5, 200)) ;; fragmentIonFUN=Function defining desired fragment ion types (e.g., b1+, y1+, b2+, y2+) ;; mascotIonScoreCutOFF=Mascot score cutoff for filtering (e.g., 17) ;; iRT=Dataframe of iRT peptides and their normalized retention times (defaults to specL::iRTpeptides) ;; fasta=FASTA object read by seqinr::read.fasta for protein annotation ;; digestPattern=Pattern for enzymatic cleavage (defaults to tryptic "(([RK])|(^)|(^M))"; use "" for semi-tryptic)
- alternatives: The documentation mentions Skyline, Peakview (AB Sciex), Spectronaut (Biognosys), and OpenSwath for targeted proteomics data analysis. specL is designed to generate libraries that can be imported into these tools.
- when_to_use: Use when you need to generate a customized, non-redundant, retention-time-normalized assay panel (spectral library) for SWATH/DIA targeted data extraction from discovery shotgun proteomics experiments.
- pitfalls: BiblioSpec files do not store protein information, so protein annotation must be performed using annotate.protein_id with a FASTA file. Database search results are heavily redundant; using them directly without redundancy filtering (e.g., via BiblioSpec/Skyline) might not result in a useful ion library. If no iRT peptides are found or provided, no iRT regression is applied, and original retention times are used instead. The default digest pattern is for tryptic peptides; for other enzymes (like semi-tryptic), digestPattern must be adapted.

workflows.name: generate_swath_spectral_library
workflows.intent: Generate a non-redundant, retention-time-normalized SWATH/DIA spectral library from BiblioSpec SQLite files and a FASTA database, and export it to a Spectronaut-compatible text file.
input: BLIB_FILTERED_FILE.sqlite (filtered BiblioSpec SQLite file containing non-redundant PSMs)
BLIB_REDUNDANT_FILE.sqlite (redundant BiblioSpec SQLite file containing all PSMs, including iRT peptides)
workflows.stages: 1. Read the filtered and redundant BiblioSpec SQLite files using read.bibliospec ;; 2. Read the FASTA file using seqinr::read.fasta ;; 3. Annotate protein IDs to the filtered PSMs using annotate.protein_id ;; 4. Define the fragment ion function ;; 5. Generate the SWATH ion library using genSwathIonLib ;; 6. Summarize and plot the generated library ;; 7. Export the library to a Spectronaut-compatible text file using write.spectronaut
workflows.code:
library(specL)

BLIB_FILTERED <- read.bibliospec(INPUT$BLIB_FILTERED_FILE) 

BLIB_REDUNDANT <- read.bibliospec(INPUT$BLIB_REDUNDANT_FILE) 

if(INPUT$ANNOTATE){
  FASTA <- read.fasta(INPUT$FASTA_FILE, 
                    seqtype = "AA", 
                    as.string = TRUE)

  BLIB_FILTERED <- annotate.protein_id(BLIB_FILTERED, 
                                       fasta = FASTA)
}

fragmentIonFunction_specL <- function (b, y) {
  Hydrogen <- 1.007825
  Oxygen <- 15.994915
  Nitrogen <- 14.003074
  b1_ <- (b )
  y1_ <- (y )
  b2_ <- (b + Hydrogen) / 2
  y2_ <- (y + Hydrogen) / 2 
  return( cbind(b1_, y1_, b2_, y2_) )
}

specLibrary <- specL::genSwathIonLib(
  data = BLIB_FILTERED,
  data.fit = BLIB_REDUNDANT,
  max.mZ.Da.error = INPUT$MZ_ERROR,
  topN = INPUT$MAX_IONS,
  fragmentIonMzRange = INPUT$FRAGMENTIONMZRANGE,
  fragmentIonRange = INPUT$FRAGMENTIONRANGE,
  fragmentIonFUN = fragmentIonFunction_specL,
  mascotIonScoreCutOFF = INPUT$MASCOTSCORECUTOFF,
  iRT = INPUT$NORMRTPEPTIDES
  )

summary(specLibrary)

plot(specLibrary)

write.spectronaut(specLibrary, file =  INPUT$OUTPUT_LIBRARY_FILE)
